Three diagrams showing carbon's bonding. Left: a single carbon atom covalently bonded to four hydrogen atoms (methane, tetrahedral shape). Middle: a straight chain of five carbon atoms bonded together with hydrogens. Right: a closed hexagonal ring of six carbon atoms.

The structural formulas of the three isomers of pentane (C5H12). Left: a straight zigzag chain of 5 carbons (pentane). Middle: a 4-carbon chain with a methyl branch on the second carbon (2-methylbutane). Right: a central carbon atom bonded to four methyl groups (2,2-dimethylpropane), forming a cross shape.

Two diagrams showing geometric isomerism in but-2-ene. Left: cis-but-2-ene, with both CH3 groups pointing upwards from the C=C double bond. Right: trans-but-2-ene, with one CH3 group pointing up and the other pointing down across the C=C double bond.

A tall fractional distillation column for crude oil. Crude oil enters a furnace at the bottom, and vapours enter the column. The column is red/hot at the bottom and blue/cool at the top. Side pipes draw off fractions. From top to bottom, labels point to: "Petroleum gases (Cooking)", "Petrol (Cars)", "Kerosene (Jets/Stoves)", "Diesel (Lorries/Generators)", "Lubricating oil", and at the very bottom "Bitumen (Roads)".

The evolution of the benzene drawing. Left side: a hexagonal ring showing alternating single and double bonds (Kekulé structure). Right side: a hexagonal ring with a complete circle drawn inside it to represent the delocalised electron cloud (Modern structure).
